description:
Filed by s527c (2026-10-31).  The EMISSION of perl's cpan/CPAN/lib/CPAN/FirstTime.pm is NOT REPRODUCIBLE: the #2610 detector table rows for its `prompt(...)` calls (lines 887, 989, 1198, ... 2125; 25 rows) read `"proto:$;$"` in some runs and `"list-call"` in others, with the SAME compiler and the SAME input; the `prompt` call bodies differ with them (e.g. a `(p-scalar (p-string-concat ...))` argument at the `Would you like me to append that to $rc now?` call in the proto runs).

Measured (s527c, 2026-10-31 00:4x-01:0x, box loaded by three agents): tools/emission-ab.pl --ref 328ebf64 over 107 files flagged FirstTime.pm DIFF (A=proto, B=list-call); a one-file re-run DIFF again; base-x (main ff5f72b5 + vendor dc242138) read 25 proto rows once and 0 in the next six runs; an extraction of 328ebf64 read 25 via probe.sh at 00:4x and 0 at 01:0x; PERL_HASH_SEED 0..7 all 0 (not hash order).  So the answer depends on time / box state, not on the compiler commit.

perl: `sub prompt ($;$)` is at line 2194, BELOW every call, so each call compiles as a plain LIST call (perl warns "called too early to check prototype") -- `list-call` is perl's reading (#2871 position-aware prototypes); the `proto:$;$` runs apply a prototype above its definition.

Suspect: something the prototype lookup reads that is not the input file (the module cache under ~/.pcl-cache shared by every tree, or a module-prototype extraction of ExtUtils::MakeMaker / CPAN::Shell with a time-dependent outcome).  Cheap discriminating measurement: run the transpile twice with PCL_CACHE_DIR=<fresh dir> vs the shared cache, and strace -e openat one proto run vs one list-call run to see which file the proto run read.
subject: CPAN/FirstTime.pm emission is not reproducible: prompt() call kind flips proto:$;$ / list-call between runs of the same compiler
